unit.why: A transmitted first-person memorate of the Apter Rav: at night an old, sick woman stands over him weeping until he must rise from his bed for her. It is a recurring event, not only a teaching.
unit.boundary_note: borderline: could also be read as a saying, since it is a habitual experience reported in his own words

stories.start_quote: בספר שער בת רבים אות פ"ג
stories.summary_en: R. Yitzhak Isaac of Zhidachov reports that the Apter Rav said that each night, after a day of Torah, worship and communal needs, an old sick woman stands over him weeping, and out of pity he is forced to rise from his bed for her.

quotes: עומדת עלי איזה זקינה וחולנית ובוכה לפני
tags.why: a waking apparition of a weeping old woman (implicitly the Shekhinah)

quotes: עומדת עלי איזה זקינה וחולנית ובוכה לפני
tags.why: an encounter with a supernatural figure who appeals to him
a female figure acts (weeps) and moves him to rise; she is symbolic rather than a real woman
the weeping and his overwhelming pity

quotes: כל היום אנו יגעין בתורה ועבודה
tags.why: his daily toil in Torah is the backdrop

quotes: שחתנו שמע מפה קדוש מורינו מוהרי״א מזידיטשוב
tags.why: the saying is framed as transmitted orally through a chain of named tellers

missing_concepts: Shekhinah in exile personified as a weeping old woman
rising at midnight (tikkun chatzot) for the Shekhinah
